title: Double-Blind, Randomized Trial Comparing the Efficacy of One-Stage versus Two-Stage Laparoscopic Transversus Abdominis Plane Block in Minimally Invasive Colon and Rectal Surgery.
summary:
This clinical study investigates whether a so-called “abdominal wall nerve block” (transversus abdominis plane block, or TAP block), performed either once or twice during minimally invasive colon or rectal surgery, is more effective at relieving pain.

The study will be conducted from April to October 2025 at the University Medical Center Mannheim. Before their surgery, patients will be randomly assigned to one of two groups—receiving either a single TAP block or a two-stage TAP block during the procedure. Neither the patients nor the medical staff involved in the evaluation will know which treatment was given (double-blinded).

In addition to measuring pain levels (e.g., on a scale from 0 to 10), the study will assess other factors such as nausea, patient satisfaction, medication use, mobility, and complications during and after surgery, up to 30 days postoperatively.

The aim is to identify the most effective method of pain management after bowel surgery—to ensure greater safety, fewer side effects, and faster recovery for patients.
conditions: Patients aged ≥18 years (ASA physical status classification I–III) undergoing elective laparoscopic or robotic colorectal surgery, with or without stoma creation, including the following procedures:  (Extended) right hemicolectomy, (Extended) left hemicolectomy, Transverse colon resection, Sigmoid resection, Subtotal colectomy (Low), anterior resection of the rectum

interventions.name: One-stage L-TAPB at the beginning of the surgery (200 mg ropivacaine)
Two-stage L-TAPB at the beginning and ending of the surgery (100 mg ropivacaine each)

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
atients aged ≥18 years undergoing elective laparoscopic or robotic colorectal surgery, with or without stoma creation, including the following procedures:  
(Extended) right hemicolectomy
(Extended) left hemicolectomy
Transverse colon resection
Sigmoid resection
Subtotal colectomy (Low)
anterior resection of the rectum

ASA physical status classification I–III
Exclusion criteria:
Language barrier
Mental or cognitive impairment preventing the patient from understanding the nature, scope, and significance of the research project
Glomerular filtration rate (GFR) < 30 mL/min
Known chronic pain conditions
Known allergies to local anesthetics
